title: Tomato Soup with Basil Oil
description: Silky roasted-tomato soup finished with bright green basil oil.
source: Sample recipe — replace with the real version from a starred chat

steps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss tomatoes, onion, and garlic with olive oil and a big pinch of salt on a sheet pan, cut sides up.
Roast until the edges char and the tomatoes collapse, about 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, make the basil oil: blanch basil in boiling water for 10 seconds, shock in ice water, squeeze bone dry.
Blend the basil with the neutral oil and a pinch of salt until vivid green, about 45 seconds. Strain through a fine sieve without pressing.
Blend the roasted vegetables with the stock until completely smooth. Work in batches and leave the blender lid vented — hot liquids erupt.
Return to the pot, warm gently, and stir in the cream if using. Season — it usually wants more salt than you think and a crack of pepper.

notes.title: Why blanch the basil
notes.body: Ten seconds of boiling water kills the enzymes that turn basil oil army-green and muddy. The ice shock locks the chlorophyll. Skip it and the oil tastes fine but looks dull by tomorrow.

notes.title: Straining without pressing
notes.body: Pressing the solids pushes fine particles through and clouds the oil. Let gravity work for ten minutes — the payoff is a jewel-clear green.

plating: Wide shallow bowls. Pour the soup, then spoon basil oil in a broken ring — it should pool in emerald islands, not blend in. One basil leaf dead center.
variations: Add a parmesan rind while the soup warms for extra depth (remove before serving).
